steps: Step 1: overhead view of a cream ceramic mixing bowl with yellow precooked corn flour partly mixed into water using a spoon. A small glass jug of water and a small salt dish nearby. No eggs in the dough.
Step 2: a single smooth supple ball of pale yellow corn dough resting in a cream ceramic bowl. Close view of moist smooth uncracked dough. No dry flour scattered over dough.

Step 3: overhead view of exactly four flat round raw pale-yellow corn dough discs, each about 12 cm wide and 6 mm thick, on food-safe transparent plastic over a wooden board. Edges smooth, a tiny reserved piece of dough aside. Not tortillas or thick bread.

Step 4: a single hollow yellow corn arepa puffing into a gently inflated round pillow in hot oil inside a deep stainless-steel pot, visibly at most half filled. Fine bubbling oil, pale golden crust, slotted metal spoon nearby. No eggs outside, no garnish.

Step 5: close view of a pale golden puffed corn arepa resting on a wooden board with a small three-centimetre slit cut only along its side edge to form a pocket; small knife beside it, no large cut through top. No egg yet.

Step 6: clear instructional closeup: one pale golden puffed corn arepa held upright with its small side opening uppermost in a cream bowl for support, a small glass spouted cup tilted to pour one raw egg with intact yolk through the side opening into its hollow centre. Natural hand pouring from cup, anatomically normal fingers. Egg is going INSIDE the arepa, not laid on top. No cooked fried egg.

Step 7: a single sealed egg-filled corn arepa on its second deep fry inside the same deep stainless steel pot of oil, golden craggy thin crust. No visible egg on exterior. Stainless slotted spoon lifting it slightly above oil, rack alongside.

Step 8 cover: beautiful finished Colombian arepas de huevo on an oval cream ceramic platter, three intact round golden-yellow gently puffed crispy corn shells and one cut in half showing a completely cooked whole egg inside: set white encasing a firm golden yolk. Thin corn crust and hollow pocket structure, not bread crumb. The egg is enclosed in the arepa, never fried egg on top. No meat, cheese, garnish, sauces or extra ingredients.
